title: Lentil Mushroom Bolognese
shortDescription: Plant-forward ragu with green lentils, cremini, and whole-wheat pasta
subtitle: Plant-forward ragu with green lentils, cremini, and whole-wheat pasta
description: Green lentils and finely chopped mushrooms simmer with tomato, wine, and herbs into a rich bolognese served over whole-wheat spaghetti.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Lentil Mushroom Bolognese in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch plant. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Cook lentils
steps.instruction: Simmer lentils in broth 20–25 minutes until tender but holding shape. Drain excess liquid so sauce does not turn watery. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts.

steps.title: Brown mushrooms
steps.instruction: Cook mushrooms in olive oil over high heat in batches 8–10 minutes until deeply browned and moisture evaporates, not gray and wet.

steps.title: Build soffritto base
steps.instruction: Sauté onion, carrot, celery 8 minutes until softened. Add garlic and tomato paste, cook 2 minutes until paste darkens to brick red.

steps.title: Simmer ragu
steps.instruction: Add wine, reduce 3 minutes. Add crushed tomatoes and cooked lentils. Simmer 20 minutes uncovered until thick and spoon-coating. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Lentil Mushroom Bolognese onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Toss with pasta
steps.instruction: Boil spaghetti al dente, drain, toss with ragu. Sauce should cling to noodles with visible mushroom and lentil pieces throughout. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Plan about 12 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

proTips: A parmesan rind simmered in sauce adds umami without meat.
Offer grated parmesan at the line for crew who want extra richness.
Sauce freezes well—thaw and toss with fresh pasta.
leftovers: Bolognese baked ziti with mozzarella top.
Lasagna layers with ricotta and sauce.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Meaty texture without meat. Budget-friendly and fiber-rich for crews trying to eat more plants.
mealPrepNotes: Pulse mushrooms in food processor for fine crumb texture. Cook lentils separately if using pre-cooked. Station: Brown mushrooms in batches—crowded mushrooms steam instead of caramelize. Station: Simmer sauce wide and uncovered so it reduces to thick ragu consistency. Station: Toss pasta with sauce in largest pot or hotel pan for even coating.
